findings.title: _start_tasks_inherited's fork point is merge-base against the operator's *current* HEAD, not the recorded cut point — if the operator's checkout later moves to a branch whose merge base with $integ lacks the inherited blobs, the original false refusal (wrong premise, inapplicable recovery) resurfaces; and in the narrow shape where HEAD contains a post-plan-apply integ commit as a non-tip ancestor (a merged mid-run snapshot, integ then advanced via a non-tasks commit such as a requirements/journal commit), the comparison reads "inherited" and silences the witness on a branch with a real plan. Both require additional failures (the roadmap witnesses lying) or unusual operator moves, so this is defense-in-depth erosion rather than a live hole, but recording the cut point at init would close it.

when the vacuity guard declines (e.g. the operator's own checkout sits on $integ, so base == tip), the refusal at libexec/orchid-start:551 still asserts "task files reach the integration branch only through 'orchid plan apply'" and offers `run resume`/`run new` — untrue and inapplicable in the genuinely-inherited shape, which is the same wrong-message defect T002 fixes elsewhere. The decline itself is the right call; the message could name the compared-against-itself case and the actual recovery (re-run from a checkout of the operator's own branch).
